1|# custom recipe: oss-fuzz build.sh needs protobuf (LPM fuzzer) which is unavailable offline;
2|# we build the plain libFuzzer harnesses exactly as expat's CMake does (ENCODING_FOR_FUZZING per encoding)
3|cd $SRC/expat/expat
4|mkdir -p b && cd b
5|cmake .. -DEXPAT_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DEXPAT_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF -DEXPAT_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DEXPAT_BUILD_DOCS=OFF \
6|  -DEXPAT_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$CC -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$CFLAGS" -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$CXX >/dev/null
7|make -j2 expat
8|LIB=$(find . -name 'libexpat*.a' | head -1)
9|for f in ../fuzz/xml_parse_fuzzer.c ../fuzz/xml_parsebuffer_fuzzer.c; do
10|  [ -f $f ] || continue
11|  b=$(basename $f .c)
12|  $CC $CFLAGS -DENCODING_FOR_FUZZING=UTF-8 -I../lib -I. -c $f -o $b.o && \
13|  $CXX $CXXFLAGS $b.o -o $OUT/${b}_UTF-8 $LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE $LIB
14|done

1|        Security fixes:
2|       #47 #1183  CVE-2026-41080 -- The existing hash flooding protection
3|                    (based on SipHash) only used 4 to 8 bytes of entropy for
4|                    a salt, when 16 bytes of salt are supported by the
5|                    implementation of SipHash used by Expat. Now full 16 bytes
6|                    of entropy are used to improve protection against hash
7|                    flooding attacks.
8|                      Existing API function XML_SetHashSalt is now deprecated
9|                    because of its limitations, and its use should be
10|                    considered a vulnerability. Please either use the new API
11|                    function XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes (with known-high-quality
12|                    entropy input only!) instead, or leave the derivation of
13|                    a 16-bytes hash salt from high quality entropy to Expat's
14|                    internal machinery (by *not* calling either of the two
15|                    XML_SetHashSalt* functions).

XML_SetHashSalt only provides 4 to 8 bytes of entropy 10| (depending on the size of type unsigned long) while the SipHash 11| implementation used by Expat can leverage up to 16 bytes of entropy — at least 12| twice as much. Function XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes of Expat >=2.7.6 14| (and where backported) matches the amount of entropy supported by SipHash. 15|
